featured_reviews.name: GURUPRASAD SHEREGAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very very poor management i have ever seen in the Indian temple. First of all not expected from our Mangalorean people.
I tried to visit this temple for the first time the road entrance was crowded and too congested so I parked my car on the main road and we started walking  the route is too dirty smelling due to mutton shops and we were tired because there were too many sun rays and  at last we reached 01:02 pm the gate was closed. We just requested management for a minute to open the gate but they denied for just 2 mins late.
Again, I tried to visit because I just believed in God and travelled by bike along with my wife and we wore masks.
We reached 12:25 pm and the day was fully special because of Rama Navami.
As per my knowledge all around the world most of the temples will not be closed till 10 pm but again the gate was closed. We asked the management person, he replied cleaning going on.
Actually this temple most people don't know then there is no need again cleaning in the afternoon only morning cleaning is enough.
Let lord Ganapathi and Punjurli bless this temple for good management 🙏.

featured_reviews.review_text: Shree Durge Parmeshwari Mata Kottee Kottee Pranam. I have been going here since my teens age and it not a single day I don’t remember Aai and Swamiji. After moving to Los Angeles as soon I land to India this is my first destination to take Darshan of Aai Durga Parmeshwari Mata and meet Swamiji. This place is divine. Just need Faith in almighty and everything will be taken care. It’s one of the Jagrut Dev mandir.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Pancha Mukhi Hanuman Temple near Civic Center Circle is a very peaceful and spiritually uplifting place. The location is excellent, making it easy for devotees to stop by for darshan while commuting to work.
Every day, thousands of people take darshan here, and the positive energy is truly calming. The maha aarti on Tuesdays and Saturdays is especially powerful and draws a large number of devotees.
A must-visit temple for anyone seeking peace, devotion, and blessings in the middle of daily life.

featured_reviews.review_text: Chakreshwar mandir is very old temple of sopara. It got old history. The Chakreshwar Mahadev Mandir is a very ancient shrine of Lord Shiva. This is a relatively small temple and is noted as the holy place where Swami Samarth performed dhyanam, pratiṣhṭha of a Ram Mandir near-by and blessed a sishya who undertook a sajiva samadhi at this very place.Sopara is one of the most historically rich cities of Maharashtra. featured_reviews.name: Shwetali Shreya Ashok
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a very ancient shrine of Lord Shiva which is located in city Nallasopara which was the largest township on India's west coast and was known by different names Sopara, Soparaka, Shurparaka, etc.
The temple is off the main road and opposite the famous Chakreshwar lake.
It is a home to most impressive idol of Lord Brahma and some other ancient sculptures.
The Brahma idol here is a standing 'Sammukha' image, wearing a 'Jata-mukuta'. Of his three faces which are seen, the middle one only has a beard. The God holds the 'Akshamala' and the 'Sruva' in the lower and upper right hands, and the 'Kamandalu' and the 'Pothi' in the lower and upper left hands.
This is a relatively small temple and is noted as the holy place where Swami Samarth performed 'Dhyanam', 'Pratiṣhṭha' of a Ram Mandir near-by and blessed their 'Shishya' Swami Mayuranand who undertook a 'Sajiva Samadhi' here.
Next to samadhi, there is an open verandah which is again a small temple where two beautifully carved sculptures are embedded in the wall.
At a temple compound wall, there are lots of stone carvings of different Hindu deity. It is said that they were all retrieved from the Chakreshwar lake, The original temple was destroyed by Portuguese who destroyed most of the temples in Bassein(Vasai) area after they took the charge from the Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.
The place is open on all days to visit.
Visiting Timings: 06:00 AM – 09:00 PM.

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
A wooden temple with fine details.

The real beauties are the 10th 11th century statues rescued from the nearby lake - the Chakreshwar talao.  These are kept in the compound for the public to appreciate, an inclusive cultural gesture.

Adjacent is another, more modern temple, housing yet more rescued sculptures.  Our guides were extremely knowledgeable about the provenance of these sculptures, which kept our group fully engaged.

The ruins of an older temple can be seen under a tarpaulin in the lane between the two temples.

featured_reviews.name: Milind Kocharekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Brahma Murti, Chakreshwar temple, Nalasopara, Mumbai, Maharashtra.

This Brahma idol was recovered from Chakreshwar talav and placed in the premises of Chakreshwar temple. As the idol is locked, I had to take pictures in parts.
This idol is three faced and the 4th face is missing.
Four faces of Brahma represents that bramha has created the world in all dimensions.
Beard (usually white) represents the maturity and experience required to create the universe.The idol in full form. Starting from the bottom left hand and going in clockwise direction, we can see Padma (Lotus) , Ledle (used mostly to serve offerings in Yajna), Book (mostly Vedas) and Kamandalam. You can see Swan which is the carrier of Brahma.

Also, you can see Ganas (association of people formed to attain the same aim, can also be called tribal people where God used to reside) in the same picture, near the legs of Brahma.You can see Toe Ring in his toe finger, which is also carved and Kadaa(an ornament) in both of his legs.
